working: Sum of coefficients of \((x-2y+3z)^n\) is obtained by setting x=y=z=1: \((1-2+3)^n = 2^n = 128 \Rightarrow n = 7\). The greatest coefficient in \((1+x)^7\) is the middle one, \(\binom{7}{3} = \binom{7}{4} = 35\).
subtopic: Coefficients and Specific Terms in Expansion

working: A five-digit number built from the five digits 0,1,2,3,4 without repetition must use all of them, so its digit sum is fixed at 0+1+2+3+4 = 10. Since 10 is not divisible by 3, no such number is divisible by 3 — no arrangement can work, so the count is 0.
notes: Not damaged, but worth flagging as a deliberate trick: the widely circulated version of this question uses the SIX digits 0,1,2,3,4,5 (sum 15, divisible by 3) and has answer 216. As printed here with only 0-4 the sum is 10 and option (D) 'No number can be found' is the mathematically correct answer. If a key says 96, the key is answering the six-digit variant, not this stem.

working: Numbers strictly between 100 and 1000 are the 3-digit numbers. With digits chosen from {5,6,7,8,9} and no repetition: 5 choices for the hundreds place, 4 for the tens, 3 for the units = 5x4x3 = 60. (No zero is available, so no leading-digit exclusion is needed.)
Total triangles from 12 points = \(\binom{12}{3} = 220\). Any 3 of the 7 collinear points are degenerate, so subtract \(\binom{7}{3} = 35\). 220 - 35 = 185.
Numbers less than 1000 from {1,2,3,4,5,6} with no repetition means 1-, 2-, or 3-digit numbers: 6 + (6x5) + (6x5x4) = 6 + 30 + 120 = 156.

Seat the 5 boys first: \(5!\) ways, creating 6 gaps (including the two ends). Place the 5 girls in 5 distinct gaps so no two are adjacent: \({}^{6}P_{5} = 6!/1! = 720 = 6!\). Total \(= 5! \times 6!\).
With \(B = -A\): \(AB = -A^2 = -A\) and \(BA = -A^2 = -A\), so \(AB+BA = -2A\). Also \((I-A)^2 = I - 2A + A^2 = I - 2A + A = I - A\). Hence the expression \(= -2A + I - (I-A) = -2A + A = -A\).

The (1,1) entry of the product is \(2(-x) + 0 + 7(x) = 5x\), which must equal 1, so \(x = 1/5\). Verified all nine entries at \(x=1/5\): (1,2) \(=28x-28x=0\), (1,3) \(=14x-14x=0\), (3,1) \(=-x+x=0\), (3,2) \(=10x-2=0\), (3,3) \(=5x=1\) — identity matrix confirmed.
For a 3x3 matrix, \(|\operatorname{adj}A| = |A|^{n-1} = 6^2 = 36\). Expanding the given adjoint: \(1(0-k) + 2(0+1) + 4(4k+1) = -k + 2 + 16k + 4 = 15k + 6\). Setting \(15k+6 = 36\) gives \(k = 2\).

Coefficient determinant \(D = \begin{vmatrix}1&1&1\\1&2&3\\1&2&\lambda\end{vmatrix} = (2\lambda-6)-(\lambda-3)+0 = \lambda-3\). Subtracting eq.2 from eq.3 gives \((\lambda-3)z = 2\): for \(\lambda \ne 3\) there is a unique solution, and at \(\lambda = 3\) it reduces to \(0 = 2\), i.e. inconsistent. So \(\lambda = 3\) is the one distinguished value, and it is the answer the option set is built around.
subtopic: Linear Systems — Consistency, Cramer's Rule, Solution Space
notes: STEM LIKELY CORRUPTED: 'is consistent?' should read 'is inconsistent?'. Taken literally, the system is consistent for EVERY \(\lambda \ne 3\), so options (A) \(\lambda=1\), (B) \(\lambda=2\) and (C) \(\lambda=-2\) are all equally correct and the question is unanswerable as printed. working: Non-trivial solutions require \(\begin{vmatrix}1&\lambda&-1\\\lambda&-1&-1\\1&1&-\lambda\end{vmatrix} = (\lambda+1) - \lambda(1-\lambda^2) - (\lambda+1) = \lambda^3 - \lambda = \lambda(\lambda-1)(\lambda+1) = 0\), i.e. \(\lambda = 0, 1, -1\) — three values. Each checked: \(\lambda=0\) gives \((t,-t,t)\), \(\lambda=1\) gives \((t,0,t)\), \(\lambda=-1\) gives \((0,t,-t)\).
subtopic: Linear Systems — Consistency, Cramer's Rule, Solution Space

working: This is the Vandermonde determinant: \(\begin{vmatrix}1&a&a^2\\1&b&b^2\\1&c&c^2\end{vmatrix} = (a-b)(b-c)(c-a)\). Numeric check at \((a,b,c)=(1,2,3)\): determinant \(= 1(18-12)-1(9-4)+1(3-2) = 2\), and \((1-2)(2-3)(3-1) = 2\). Option (B) is wrong (at (1,2,3) it gives \((1-4)(4-9)(9-1) = 120\)) and (C) is wrong (\((1-2+3)(2-3+1)(3-1+2) = 0\)).
notes: OPTIONS DAMAGED: option (A) is printed EMPTY, and its text has leaked above the option block as an orphan truncated line — 'a. (a -- b) (b -- c) (c --'. The source clearly meant option (A) = \((a-b)(b-c)(c-a)\), truncated mid-factor at '(c --' where '(c - a)' should close. So the derived value \((a-b)(b-c)(c-a)\) belongs to label A. working: Split the third column: \(\Delta = \begin{vmatrix}x&x^2&1\\y&y^2&1\\z&z^2&1\end{vmatrix} + \begin{vmatrix}x&x^2&x^3\\y&y^2&y^3\\z&z^2&z^3\end{vmatrix}\). A cyclic column shift (even permutation) makes the first \(=(x-y)(y-z)(z-x)\); factoring x, y, z from the rows makes the second \(= xyz\,(x-y)(y-z)(z-x)\). So \(\Delta = (x-y)(y-z)(z-x)(1+xyz) = (\ldots)(1-1) = 0\).
A non-zero (non-trivial) solution needs \(\begin{vmatrix}1&-k&-1\\k&-1&-1\\1&1&-1\end{vmatrix} = 1(1+1) + k(1-k) - (k+1) = 2 + k - k^2 - k - 1 = 1 - k^2 = 0\), so \(k = \pm 1\).
subtopic: Linear Systems — Consistency, Cramer's Rule, Solution Space

working: Vieta on \(x^3+ax^2+0\cdot x+b=0\): \(\sum\alpha = -a\), \(\sum\alpha\beta = 0\), \(\alpha\beta\gamma = -b\). The circulant determinant equals \(3\alpha\beta\gamma - (\alpha^3+\beta^3+\gamma^3) = -(\sum\alpha)(\sum\alpha^2 - \sum\alpha\beta)\). Here \(\sum\alpha^2 = (-a)^2 - 2(0) = a^2\), so the value \(= -(-a)(a^2) = a^3\). Verified numerically on the cubic \(x^3-1.5x^2+0.5\) (roots 1, 1, -0.5, so \(a=-1.5\)): determinant \(= 3(1)(1)(-0.5)-1-1+0.125 = -3.375 = (-1.5)^3\).
subtopic: Special Determinants — Trig, Complex, Roots of Unity, Polynomial

working: With the (3,1) entry equal to 0, \(\Delta = C(C^2-1) - 1(C-0) = C^3 - 2C\). Substituting \(C = 2\cos\theta\): \(8\cos^3\theta - 4\cos\theta = 4\cos\theta(2\cos^2\theta - 1) = 4\cos\theta\cos 2\theta = \frac{2\sin 2\theta\cos 2\theta}{\sin\theta} = \frac{\sin 4\theta}{\sin\theta}\).
subtopic: Special Determinants — Trig, Complex, Roots of Unity, Polynomial

working: Half-angle substitution: numerator \(= 2\sin^2\frac{A}{2} + 2\sin\frac{A}{2}\cos\frac{A}{2} = 2\sin\frac{A}{2}(\sin\frac{A}{2}+\cos\frac{A}{2})\); denominator \(= 2\cos^2\frac{A}{2} + 2\sin\frac{A}{2}\cos\frac{A}{2} = 2\cos\frac{A}{2}(\cos\frac{A}{2}+\sin\frac{A}{2})\). Ratio \(= \tan\frac{A}{2}\). Numeric check \(A=90^\circ\): \((1+1-0)/(1+1+0) = 1 = \tan 45^\circ\).

Divide numerator and denominator by \(\csc^2 15^\circ\): \(\frac{\cot^2 x - 1}{\cot^2 x + 1} = \frac{\cos^2 x - \sin^2 x}{\cos^2 x + \sin^2 x} = \cos 2x\). So the value is \(\cos 30^\circ = \frac{\sqrt3}{2}\). Numeric check: \(\cot 15^\circ = 2+\sqrt3\), \(\cot^2 15^\circ = 7+4\sqrt3 \approx 13.9282\), giving \(12.9282/14.9282 \approx 0.8660\).

Acute angles give \(\sin\theta = 4/5\), \(\sin\phi = 3/5\). Then \(\cos(\theta-\phi) = \frac{3}{5}\cdot\frac{4}{5} + \frac{4}{5}\cdot\frac{3}{5} = \frac{24}{25}\), so \(\cos^2\frac{\theta-\phi}{2} = \frac{1+24/25}{2} = \frac{49}{50}\) and \(\cos\frac{\theta-\phi}{2} = \frac{7}{\sqrt{50}} = \frac{7}{5\sqrt2}\) (positive, since \(\frac{\theta-\phi}{2}\) is small). Note (A) \(7/\sqrt2 \approx 4.95\) and (C) \(7/\sqrt5 \approx 3.13\) exceed 1 and are impossible for a cosine.

\(\frac{\sin\theta}{1-\cot\theta} = \frac{\sin^2\theta}{\sin\theta-\cos\theta}\) and \(\frac{\cos\theta}{1-\tan\theta} = \frac{\cos^2\theta}{\cos\theta-\sin\theta}\). Sum \(= \frac{\sin^2\theta-\cos^2\theta}{\sin\theta-\cos\theta} = \sin\theta+\cos\theta\). Numeric check \(\theta=30^\circ\): \(0.5/(1-1.7321) + 0.8660/(1-0.5774) = -0.6830 + 2.0490 = 1.3660 = \sin30^\circ+\cos30^\circ\).
